scope: For neighboring wires the two-qubit SWAP matrix maps the dense amplitude to the amplitude with the input bits exchanged. Applying it twice restores the state.
An addressed invertible two-qubit gate retains its left inverse; inserting SWAPs before and after it preserves invertibility throughout the circuit.
Routing bookkeeping identifies both physical target bits and the basis input after replacing only those bits. Adding a spectator preserves its value throughout the route.
Routing inserts one outward and one return SWAP per skipped site and one central gate. A single arbitrary-pair operation compiles to at most 2n adjacent operations on n qubits.
Vidal’s nonconsecutive-gate routing step before Theorem 1. The dense action of the compiled SWAP sequence is exactly the intended matrix action on the selected original pair.
Every pair of numerical positions i < j < n occurs among the simulator’s addresses, including the two ends of the chain.
Coordinates of computational-basis strings agree with the explicit wire permutation of a nearest-neighbor SWAP. The indexing permutation is its own inverse.
Vidal Eq. (2) bounds Schmidt rank over every bipartition. Prefix/suffix coefficient matrices over every permutation express this bound, so each SWAP inherits it on every cut.
All intermediate states introduced by routing are wire permutations of the pre- or post-gate logical state. A physical rank bound on the original circuit suffices throughout the adjacent simulation.
An entire program on arbitrary qubit pairs compiles to an exactly equivalent adjacent circuit of invertible gates of length at most 2nG for G original operations.
A one-wire operation acts with an identity on its unused neighbor. Encoding mixed circuits this way preserves dense evolution, invertibility and the rank promises at the original gate boundaries.

From a nonzero product input and physical all-bipartition rank bound χ, the actual routed simulation on n ≥ 2 wires gives the dense final product expectation. Work including readout is ≤ 2nG(24χ³ + 40χ²) + n(20χ³ + 8χ²); peak scalar storage is ≤ 2nχ² + 36χ² + 4χ.
Singleton-register base case: arbitrary sequences reduce to ordinary matrix–vector products in two amplitudes, with eight scalar operations per gate.

Theorem 1, all widths in the scalar-arithmetic model. Given nonzero product input and G arbitrary one- or two-qubit invertible gates, χ bounds the physical Schmidt ranks across all bipartitions at the original steps. An explicit classical algorithm returns the exact product-observable expectation in ≤ 200(G+1)(n+1)(χ+1)³ operations and ≤ 100(n+1)(χ+1)² scalar slots. This includes local Born projectors on normalized states and all unitary circuits. The paper’s separate finite-precision discussion is in note [10].
